title.narrative: Output 7.3. Increased capacity of Member States to set adequate wages and promote decent working time

description.narrative: Compliance with national provisions on working time in the assessed factories improved significantly. In 2022, the rate of non-compliance was particularly low as regards rest breaks (8 per cent), daily rest (1 per cent), and there was no evidence of non-compliance with provisions on annual leave. As part of the continued efforts to improve the working conditions in the garment and footwear sectors, technical support and advice were provided to over 480 factories with a total workforce of 760,000 workers so that they could improve compliance with the national regulations on working hours, rest time and annual leave, especially in the context of post-COVID 19 and shrinking business due to low aggregate demand.

Output 2.4. Increased capacity Member States to apply sectoral international labour standards, codes of practice and guidelines

description.narrative:
The Government of Viet Nam, together with employers and workers organizations, developed, implemented, and advocated for best practices in the electronics manufacturing industry.
In particular: - The Ministry of Labour - Invalids and Social Affairs (MOLISA) developed a research report on the regulation of digital employment contracts, with significant inputs from Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry (VCCI) and Vietnam General Confederation of Labour (VGCL) and electronics factories management and workers. This research forms the basis for new guidelines for businesses, workers, and local labour agencies. - Quarterly sectoral consultation meetings are being held to promote social dialogue. - VCCI and VGCL conducted 13 training courses for electronics factory representatives, covering topics such as soft skills, industrial relations, freedom of association, collective bargaining, and occupational safety and health; 447 participants (67% women) from the industry attended these programmes. - VCCI scaled up the use of a self-facilitated, activity-based learning approach in the electronics sector, which helps manufacturers improve productivity, competitiveness, and working conditions. - VGCL adapted training materials on sexual harassment prevention and conducted a Training of Trainers program. With funding support from EU and APPLE Inc. in coordination with VCCI, the ILO published the research report on Vietnam’s electronics supply chain in January 2023. The ILO also provided MOLISA information on good practices to mainstream gender equality in labour inspection for the electronics industry. With the support of the SSN fund, the ILO and VCCI co-hosted quarterly tripartite sectoral consultation meetings at both national and provincial levels. 6 meetings were organized in the period between November 2021- April 2023. The ILO provided VCCI information on good practices on gender mainstreaming and facilitated policy guidance on the new legal article on digital labour contracts as stipulated in the Labour Code to MOLISA. Building on existing training tools, materials developed for garment and footwear factories of the ILO/IFC Programme were adapted to fit the electronics supply chain audience. The ILO also developed a list of FAQs on the Labour Code 2019 in English and Vietnamese to support enterprises in its application, and organized industry seminars on working time and wage policies, gender equality, and labor subleasing practices. Three eLearning courses were developed on sustainable compliance in the electronics industry, based on BetterWork and other ILO materials. Finally, the ILO provided technical support to tripartite partners to adopt good practices on the sustainable compliance model and pilot the use of ILO tools/materials in sectoral interventions.
